component.name: TuxDisplay
component.summary: Extend a GNOME Wayland desktop to an iPad or Android tablet over USB

description.p: TuxDisplay creates a native GNOME Wayland extended monitor and streams it directly to compatible OpenDisplay apps on iPadOS and Android over USB without requiring an IP network.
An authenticated browser receiver remains available for private networks and compatibility use.
Desktop sessions without the required GNOME virtual-monitor APIs use an isolated X11 workspace rather than extending the current desktop.
One graphical application provides the manager and tray indicator, including verified in-app updates from GitHub Releases.

Stop safely after a service failure instead of recreating the virtual monitor in a loop.
Reload the user service definition during in-app updates.

Restore the complete monitor layout under stable identities.
Validate saved geometry before applying it through Mutter.
Prevent restored tablet placement from overlapping another display.
Keep PipeWire running while GNOME display positions change.
Refresh OpenDisplay without a GStreamer state transition.
Prevent frozen video and slow shutdown after rearrangement.
Remember the tablet monitor arrangement across service restarts.
Refresh PipeWire and OpenDisplay after GNOME monitor-layout changes.
Keep the virtual monitor alive while displays are rearranged.
Add Android OpenDisplay support through a device-scoped ADB USB tunnel.
Show Android authorization and receiver connection states.
Keep video, input, reconnect, and offline behavior consistent across iPadOS and Android.
Unify the manager and tray indicator in one single-instance application.

Add verified in-app updates from GitHub Releases.
